question: FX-6: would int32 weights + SIMD inference speed the product up?
method: stage timings (median of 7 fresh processes) of unisacc.com vs the classic table-lookup reference on examples/apps/calc.c
Time Profiler samples of a symbolised private executor (exec/c/run.c -O2 -g) running the E2 network on the 1.3 MB flattened compiler source
same executor built -O2 / -O3 / -O3 -mcpu=native -fvectorize -fslp-vectorize, median of 7 on the same input
instrumented copy of core_transition counting transitions and the active-unit prefix length (cut) per transition
facts: weights are already int (next/seq arrays); the transition is a binary search over ascending thresholds plus a prefix sum of the active units
the average prefix is 1.9 units: there is no dot product to vectorise; O3/native auto-vectorisation changes nothing (234.7 -> 238 ms)
the product is ~15x slower than the classic table route on calc (129 vs 8 ms): the cost is ~10 ns of fixed overhead per transition times ~18 transitions per input byte, not arithmetic width
conclusion: int32 + SIMD would not reach the 15% end-to-end bar; the levers are fewer transitions per byte (wider observations, run-length actions) and cheaper transitions (bank locality, branchless prefix search, fused seq/next arrays). Registered as a negative result for the paper (T-4 discussion) and as R13 candidate work items.
paper_note: T-4 stands as stated: the representation is free to change (int32 today, could be int8 or SIMD) without touching kernel semantics; but the measured profile says representation width is not where the time goes.
